rule: GOAL: Fill four empty slots with colored tokens to match the target sequence displayed at the top of the screen. CONTROLS: Click a color in the bottom palette to select it, then click a middle slot to place that color inside. RULE: Tokens must be placed in the exact left-to-right order shown by the hollow squares at the top: blue, green, yellow, purple. TRAP: Believing you could place tokens in any order or that the gray placeholders in the palette were obstacles, rather than just swap targets.

GOAL: Align the sliding blocks to fit the wall gap. CONTROLS: Click blue handles to shift top and bottom sections horizontally. RULE: One click moves both sections in opposite directions by four units. TRAP: Assuming sections move independently wastes time; they are mechanically linked.

GOAL: Guide the square to the socket by moving it along the diagonal trail. CONTROLS: Clicking a trail dot moves the square along the path toward that spot. RULE: The square moves exactly six steps per click, regardless of where you click on the trail. TRAP: Clicking near the square wastes moves; always aim for the farthest valid dot within range.

GOAL: Fill the middle pocket with white fluid to power the piston rightward. CONTROLS: Upper handles pump fluid down through walls; lower handles pump fluid up or move pistons. RULE: Fluid flows from larger regions to smaller ones, enabling sequential transfers between zones. TRAP: Clicking the piston handle before filling the middle pocket wastes actions because it needs fuel to move.

GOAL: Guide the blue node to the exit by sliding across the grid. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player exactly two tiles in that direction. RULE: Each step must land two tiles away; you cannot stop early or change direction mid-slide. TRAP: Assuming you can stop after one tile or block movement with obstacles costs time; plan for rigid two-tile jumps.

GOAL: Arrange colored tokens into matching slots. CONTROLS: Click a token to pick it up, then click a target slot to place or swap it. Press space to finish the level. RULE: Clicking a filled slot while holding a token swaps them, allowing you to rotate groups without empty spaces. TRAP: Assuming you must move tokens to an empty spot first. You do not; direct swapping is the efficient path.

GOAL: Guide a two-part snake to push boxes into empty frame slots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the whole snake; Space absorbs or deposits a box at the head. RULE: The head always stays on top when carrying, so deposits occur at the head cell. TRAP: Forgetting that UP blocks movement if a box sits above the head forces detours.

GOAL: Arrange seven colored tokens in the target sequence. CONTROLS: Click palette colors, then click empty slots to place them. Press space to confirm. RULE: Read the main row left to right, inserting connected sub-boxes at their marked ring positions. TRAP: Assuming all slots fill sequentially ignores that sub-boxes interrupt the main row’s order.

GOAL: Arrange colored tokens to match a hidden target sequence across two linked boxes. CONTROLS: Click a palette token, then click a slot to place it; press Space to confirm. RULE: A ring connector bridges the boxes, merging their slots into one continuous reading order. TRAP: Assuming ring slots are color slots; they only connect, so place the ring before filling colors.

GOAL: Arrange colored tokens to match a target sequence by inserting repeating blocks. CONTROLS: Click palette items to select, then click board slots to place them. Press space to submit. RULE: Blue rings act as wildcards, repeating the adjacent blue block to fill multiple target positions. TRAP: Assuming every ring covers a single slot wastes moves; rings can expand to cover multiple matching segments.

GOAL: Align each slot’s glyph to its target class using the global order. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor between slots and cycle glyphs up or down. RULE: Moving forward or backward in the class list costs the fewest presses. TRAP: Assuming the glyph order is identical in every slot wastes time verifying.

GOAL: Move the large square to the top-left corner to merge with the small square. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell moves the square so its center lands on that cell. RULE: The square travels a fixed distance per click, requiring multiple steps to cross the grid. TRAP: Assuming one click can reach distant targets wastes time; you must plan a multi-step path.

GOAL: Match the target color sequence by arranging rings and filling color slots. CONTROLS: Click rings to place them in red slots; click colors to fill box slots; press space to submit. RULE: Ring order dictates the sequence, so place rings to align each box’s starting color with the target. TRAP: Ignoring pre-filled starting colors leads to mismatched sequences; always verify the first color matches the target’s first item.

GOAL: Move the paddle under the tap and pour water to hit the yellow target. CONTROLS: Arrows move the paddle; Space pours water. RULE: The paddle must be positioned directly beneath the water source before pouring. TRAP: Thinking the paddle needs to catch falling water; it must be ready under the tap when you press Space.

GOAL: Transfer white liquid from bottom to top using handles. CONTROLS: Click handles to move two rows of liquid between adjacent columns. RULE: Liquid flows downhill; plan the chain so sources empty into sinks without overflow. TRAP: Assuming direct paths work; you must often push liquid into intermediate columns to clear space for higher transfers.

GOAL: Guide the block into the socket below. CONTROLS: Click glyph segments to set directions; click the run button to execute moves. RULE: A horizontal dash on top moves left; a vertical dash on the bottom moves down. TRAP: Assuming all dashes act independently; combining top and bottom segments creates a single downward command, not a left-down sequence.

GOAL: Identify the seven unique glyph classes and match the target class to the correct slot option. CONTROLS: Arrow keys navigated between slot options to verify class matches. RULE: Only glyphs sharing the same class as the target slot were valid solutions. TRAP: Assuming exact key matches were required, when only class equivalence mattered for validation.

GOAL: Build a nested color sequence using boxes and rings. CONTROLS: Click two spots to swap items; Space to reset. RULE: Rings hold tokens; their color defines the inner pattern. TRAP: Ignoring that ring colors dictate the contained sequence.

ESTABLISHED: The plug oscillates size (16 to 4 cells) each entry, advancing two columns every two entries. Keypad entries flash purple then reset regardless of orientation. FAILED: Assuming the plug size cycle indicates linear progress toward a left-side target. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the blade's left end via standard movement, nor matching keypad colors to the panel. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate plug orientation; keypad clicks toggle cells; entries trigger size shifts and positional advances.

GOAL: Guide the player to the exit while avoiding the patrolling guard. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one step per press. RULE: The guard blocks movement but only fires when the player is in the same row within two cells. TRAP: Assuming the guard blocks all line-of-sight attacks; it actually permits safe vertical approach from the side.

ESTABLISHED: Moving the avatar up releases block b but threads block R. Moving down carries R to the target row but re-threads b. FAILED: Retracting the wire while b is threaded drags b left into the dock. GOAL IS NOT: Simply parking b in the target row, as it must remain rightmost. CONTROLS: UP/Down shifts the wire's vertical position; Left/Right adjusts the wire's horizontal span.

GOAL: Match the answer row’s seven slots to the target shapes derived from the source pairs. CONTROLS: Arrows cycled through available shape options for the selected slot. RULE: Each source pair contributed specific shape types, defining the exact sequence needed for the solution. TRAP: Assuming shape classes were unique by name; rotations of the same shape count as identical, requiring careful matching.

GOAL: Transform blue glyphs into yellow glyphs by passing them through two distinct transformation stages. CONTROLS: Arrow keys cycle the selected glyph option to match the required output shape. RULE: Apply the first mapping to get pink, then the second mapping to get yellow. TRAP: Assuming a direct blue-to-yellow map ignores the intermediate pink state, causing mismatched outputs.

GOAL: Navigate the grid from start to finish while avoiding hazards. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one step per press. RULE: Red tiles attack horizontally if the player enters their line of sight. TRAP: Assuming safety just because you are not directly in front of a hazard; side alignment triggers attacks.

GOAL: Slide two markers to align with red cross targets. CONTROLS: Click side buttons to move horizontal marker; click top/bottom buttons to move vertical marker. RULE: Match each marker’s color to its corresponding panel and slider. TRAP: Assuming red crosses are hazards; they are actually the required endpoints.

GOAL: Align two colored crosshairs with their target dots by moving them across the grid. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active crosshair three cells per press. Spacebar switches control between yellow and blue crosshairs. RULE: Each arrow press moves the cross exactly three cells, allowing rapid alignment with distant targets. TRAP: Do not assume one press equals one cell; calculating moves as single steps wastes time and actions.

GOAL: Align three shapes onto their target dot clusters. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active shape three units per press. Spacebar cycles focus to the next shape. RULE: Only the shape with the white marker moves; others remain stationary until selected. TRAP: Assuming spacebar is free. It consumes one action budget, so switch shapes sparingly.

GOAL: Move the yellow block to the highlighted corner slot. CONTROLS: Click the red arrow to rotate the entire ring of blocks. RULE: The ring shifts one step per click; choose the direction with the fewest moves. TRAP: Thinking the green arrow was necessary; it was merely a distractor for this level.

GOAL: Position the connecting blob precisely inside the target ring. CONTROLS: Clicking a colored gem moves it to that spot; clicking the other gem swaps their positions. RULE: The blob always sits exactly halfway between the two gems, so you must align their midpoint with the ring. TRAP: Thinking you win by placing a single gem in the ring; only the midpoint matters, so ignore individual gem locations.

GOAL: Place three shapes onto matching dot patterns within a strict action limit. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the active shape three squares per press; Space cycles the active shape. RULE: Each shape covers exactly its target dots; moves are rigid, not sliding. TRAP: Assuming one press moves one square; each arrow press jumps three squares, so plan accordingly.

GOAL: Clear the board by moving pegs into empty spots. CONTROLS: Click a peg to select it, then click a highlighted landing spot to jump. RULE: A peg jumps over an adjacent peg into the empty space immediately beyond it. TRAP: Assuming you need to click twice per move; one click selects, the next executes.

GOAL: Navigate the rectangular block to the exit box while matching the required glyph orientation. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the block five grid units per press, regardless of facing direction. RULE: Passing over the plus symbol rotated the block, changing its active collision shape. TRAP: Assuming movement distance depended on the block's orientation caused unnecessary pathing detours.

GOAL: Guide two separate characters to meet at the single top-center opening to merge them. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the left character directly, while simultaneously mirroring the right character’s horizontal direction. RULE: Vertical moves apply identically to both, but left and right inputs flip horizontally for the second character. TRAP: Assuming both characters move independently or that horizontal controls affect them in the same direction.

GOAL: Align yellow markers to target slots on row 26. CONTROLS: Click orange arrows to shift row 26 left; click green arrows to shift row 26 right. RULE: Orange and green arrows perform opposite cyclic shifts on the same row. TRAP: Assuming green arrows do nothing or affect a different row wasted time verifying their inverse effect.

GOAL: Match the highlighted panel’s tiles to the pattern shown in its center dial. CONTROLS: Click individual tiles to toggle their color between red and blue. RULE: Only the highlighted panel is active; white dial marks require red tiles, gray marks require blue. TRAP: Assuming all panels are interactive; clicking solved panels wastes moves and ignores the single active target.

GOAL: The goal was to extend the snake-like chain until its head reached the target dot. CONTROLS: Clicking the four segments extended that specific part of the chain by three units. RULE: Segments had to grow in a strict order to avoid overlapping or hitting the walls. TRAP: I wrongly thought I could extend any segment at any time, causing invalid moves.

GOAL: Turn specific grid cells orange to match the dial patterns, keeping others blue. CONTROLS: Clicking a tile cycles its color between blue and orange. RULE: Dial whites indicate orange targets; grays indicate blue; the dial center color defines the target hue. TRAP: Assuming panels operate independently; they share a middle row, so changes affect both dials’ constraints simultaneously.

GOAL: Match each shape’s color to its dots by first touching the correct colored square, then covering the matching dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active shape; Space switches between the X and the plus sign. RULE: A shape permanently takes the color of the square it last covered, even after moving away. TRAP: Assuming color changes are temporary or that shapes must stay on the square to affect the dots.

GOAL: Guide both players to merge at the center point to clear the level. CONTROLS: Arrows move the left player directly; the right player mirrors every move horizontally. RULE: One control drives two characters simultaneously, requiring synchronized movement through shared corridors. TRAP: Assuming both players face the same direction causes crashes; remember the right player’s left is your right.

GOAL: Place yellow and orange blocks onto their matching colored markers. CONTROLS: Click left or right column to rotate loops independently. RULE: Each loop rotates fully; shared slots affect both colors simultaneously. TRAP: Assuming loops are independent; they intersect, so rotating one shifts blocks in the other.

GOAL: Paint all tiles to match their required colors. CONTROLS: Click a tile to flip its color. RULE: Each dial shows the target color for tiles in its range; white means use the panel's ink, gray means use the opposite. TRAP: Assuming gray meant neutral or empty; it strictly means the other available color.

GOAL: Place both squares into their matching ring sockets to open the gate. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active square; clicking a square makes it active. RULE: Rings are passable, allowing squares to slide through overlapping areas to reach targets. TRAP: Assuming arrows control all squares; they only move the one with the white dot, requiring clicks to switch focus.

GOAL: Guide two distinct blocks to their specific, color-coded target slots on the grid. CONTROLS: Click directional arrows to shift entire rows or columns, moving all blocks within that line simultaneously. RULE: Each block moves independently along its path; you must align both to their respective goals without disturbing the other once placed. TRAP: Assuming single-block movement. Clicks affect whole lines, so a move intended for one block often displaces the other, requiring complex sequencing.

GOAL: Match the dial patterns to color the grid cells correctly. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell cycled its color between blue, orange, and red. RULE: Every white spot on a dial demanded that specific color in the grid. TRAP: Assuming gray dial spots allowed any color, when they actually forbade the dial's own color.

ESTABLISHED: A gray block previously traced a prior path from start to end. FAILED: Replaying specific moves or resetting did not trigger the ghost in recent attempts. GOAL IS NOT: Simply matching previous move sequences or visiting specific coordinates. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player; SPACE resets the level to the starting position.

GOAL: Merge two colored pairs into their target centers. CONTROLS: Click empty space to move cursor; click gray diamond to swap positions. RULE: A pair forms when the cursor sits between two matching dots; the swap moves the cursor to the gray spot. TRAP: Assuming you must move dots directly; you only move the cursor to define the merge point.

GOAL: Move the cart to park beside the peg, then jump it into the empty slot. CONTROLS: Click the cart to select, click the destination to move, click the landing spot to jump. RULE: The cart carries the peg; the peg only moves when the cart lands adjacent to it. TRAP: Thinking you can drop the peg directly into the panel; you must carry it to the edge first.

GOAL: Reach the goal before energy runs out. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move. RULE: Collect the refill item to extend your range. TRAP: Thinking you can reach the goal directly; the distance exceeds your starting energy.

GOAL: Move yellow blocks into marked slots to clear the level. CONTROLS: Clicking arrows rotates blocks along a specific path. RULE: Blocks shift one step along the track; empty spaces do not count as stops. TRAP: Assuming all visible slots are part of the active cycle wastes time tracking static blocks.

GOAL: Move the gray piece to the target by swapping with the cursor. CONTROLS: Click to move the cursor; clicking the piece swaps it with the cursor. RULE: The blob centers between the piece and cursor, so position them to guide the path. TRAP: Believing you must click the piece directly; you actually click its current location to swap it away.

GOAL: Turn all grid cells purple by satisfying the numeric clues on the dials. CONTROLS: Click empty cells to flip their color; click special toggler cells to flip themselves and adjacent neighbors. RULE: The numbers on the dials indicate exactly how many adjacent cells must be purple when solved. TRAP: Assuming dial cells themselves could be clicked or counted as purple; they are static obstacles that only provide constraints.

GOAL: Align the plug’s prongs with the socket to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the plug piece horizontally or vertically one step at a time. RULE: The plug only fits when its prongs face the socket and align perfectly with the holes. TRAP: Thinking rotation was needed; the plug was already facing the correct direction, so only movement was required.

GOAL: Slide the block to fit its pattern into the target zone. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block one step per press. RULE: Match the dot spacing exactly to the guide lines. TRAP: Assuming dots stay fixed while sliding; they align relative to the block’s center, not the grid.

GOAL: Guide three separate color chains to their matching endpoint targets without collision. CONTROLS: Click a chain's entry to swap its starting position, then click the target to move the blob one step. RULE: Each chain must be routed sequentially; one blob moves fully before the next begins to avoid grid overlap. TRAP: Assuming you can interleave moves between chains; this causes immediate blockage and wastes actions.

GOAL: Guide the charcoal to cover the hidden yellow zone. CONTROLS: Arrows move pieces; Space toggles control modes. RULE: Mode one moves charcoal naturally while black stays put; mode two mirrors movement for both pieces. TRAP: Assuming black always moves with charcoal wastes turns; remember to toggle modes to keep black stationary during horizontal alignment.

GOAL: Cover all target dots using three shapes. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected shape. Space switches the active shape. RULE: Each shape must change color to match the dots it covers. TRAP: Assuming the white center marker is always visible; overlapping shapes hide it, causing confusion about the active piece’s location.

GOAL: Match tile colors to targets by cycling states. CONTROLS: Arrows move cursor; UP cycles state forward; DOWN cycles backward. RULE: Seven UPs return to start, so map the cycle once to deduce exact steps. TRAP: Assuming linear distance; wrapping or state cycles require precise counting, not just shortest path.

ESTABLISHED: Moving the core near the red bar triggers a 90-degree rotation that shifts it upward, bypassing the blue block's usual trap. FAILED: Directly pushing the core into the blue square or standard paths leads to a no-op animation and no progress. GOAL IS NOT: The exit is not located at the initial starting point or behind the static gray barriers. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the core. Clicking red bars rotates them. Clicking blue squares toggles their solidity.

ESTABLISHED: Down moves clockwise, Up moves counter-clockwise. Left and Right also rotate the tool. Space applies paint. FAILED: Up at the top or upper-right did nothing. Left at upper-left did nothing. GOAL IS NOT: The goal is not simply reaching the bottom; you must paint specific halves. CONTROLS: Down orbits clockwise. Up orbits counter-clockwise. Left rotates left. Right rotates right. Space paints.

ESTABLISHED: A vertical water channel now connects the upper rectangle to the lower band. Walls at specific column intervals block horizontal movement in the top strip. Green blocks sit in distinct clusters above and below the main water body. FAILED: Trying to access left-side blocks from the right-side water rectangle. Assuming walls disappear when adjacent blocks are removed. Believing the top strip was directly accessible from the middle band. GOAL IS NOT: Breaking the solid wall rows immediately adjacent to the water. Clearing the entire top strip of green blocks. CONTROLS: Clicking a gre

GOAL: Paint the stack's upper half white. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate the piston around the stack; clicks select color; Space paints. RULE: Piston position dictates paint coverage, so align it to the top before painting. TRAP: Assuming arrow keys move the piston freely rather than rotating it in fixed slots.

GOAL: Reach the yellow core by navigating obstacles. CONTROLS: Arrows move the core; clicks toggle red and blue pieces. RULE: Pieces only move if the core is not on their source or destination cells. TRAP: Assuming the core blocks a toggle if near the piece; it only blocks if directly on top.

GOAL: Paint the top purple, bottom-right orange, leaving the bottom-left white. CONTROLS: Space applies the current color to the region under the active piston. Arrow keys rotate the piston’s position. Clicks select colors. RULE: Press the bottom-right piston last so its orange overlay corrects any purple spills into the diagonal boundary. TRAP: Assuming the bottom-left needs painting; it starts white and remains untouched if you skip that step.

GOAL: Guide the yellow core through a winding corridor to its glowing target spot. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the core two grid units per press, jumping over gaps. RULE: The core can only land on solid blocks, requiring precise two-step alignment to navigate corners. TRAP: Believing the core moves one unit causes overshooting targets and getting stuck in dead-end corridors.

GOAL: Guide scattered dots to parking spots, then merge two players. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active piece; clicks select a new target. RULE: Selecting a dot updates the active index, not just the visual highlight. TRAP: Assuming selection order stays fixed causes moves to apply to the wrong dot.

GOAL: Move the small square to the top-right corner. CONTROLS: Clicking anywhere pulls the nearest square toward that spot. RULE: The square moves to the clicked location only if it is closer to the click than any other square. TRAP: Believing you can drag the square directly; clicking near the destination often pulls the wrong square if it is even slightly closer to the cursor.

GOAL: Paint the stacked pistons to match the target pattern, accounting for the small piston orbiting the large one. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate the assembly; mouse clicks select colors or press pistons; SPACE applies the selected color. RULE: Rotating the assembly moves both pistons together, keeping their relative positions fixed while changing which cells they cover. TRAP: Ignoring the small piston’s orbit causes it to paint the wrong cells or hide inside the large piston’s region.

GOAL: Navigate to the exit while dodging a patrolling enemy. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the player one step per turn. RULE: The enemy moved simultaneously, so you had to predict its next position before moving. TRAP: Thinking the health bar was flexible; it was a hard limit, meaning any collision instantly ended the attempt.

GOAL: Place four colors to match the target pattern. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate the view; clicking a swatch selects a color; clicking the device places it. RULE: The small piston creates a four-row block when rotated left. TRAP: Assuming the yellow target was three rows high wasted time on incorrect rotation steps.

GOAL: Cross the grid while avoiding patrolling enemies. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved your character one step per turn. RULE: Enemies slide two spaces per turn, bouncing off walls and passing through each other. TRAP: Assuming enemies stop or collide with one another, rather than continuing their full patrol path.

GOAL: Move two pieces to merge into one. CONTROLS: Arrows move both pieces simultaneously; clicks swap their positions. RULE: A merge occurs only when both pieces land on the exact same coordinate. TRAP: Assuming the path is valid if the final state looks close; always verify the last move actually connects them.

GOAL: Align three gray markers to form a triangle around the target blob. CONTROLS: Move the cursor; click a marker to swap it with the cursor. RULE: The cursor is global; swapping attaches it to that chain, leaving a gray at its old spot. TRAP: Assuming chains have separate cursors. Swapping with the wrong chain moves your shared cursor unexpectedly.

ESTABLISHED: The paddle slides until blocked; liquid spreads beneath it. FAILED: Placing the paddle above bars without a sandwiched liquid layer triggered no swap. GOAL IS NOT: Simply filling notches without a color exchange; nor is it avoiding the ceiling. CONTROLS: Arrows slide the paddle; SPACE pours liquid, swapping paddle and bar colors if liquid is trapped between them.

GOAL: Move the mirrored piece fully above the hidden line to complete the level. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the active piece; Space toggles selection and mode. RULE: Selected pieces move three steps per press; unselected pieces move six steps. TRAP: Assuming reflections are static or clipped; they move with the piece and can cross the line visually.

GOAL: Slide the yellow token to the vertical ray's outer tip, then swap all tokens into marked slots. CONTROLS: The bottom button rotates the ring; the mid-left button extends the ray outward; the center button swaps tokens. RULE: Ring rotation moves the token along the perimeter, while the ray button pushes it from the second position to the third. TRAP: Assuming the ray button works from any position; it only advances the token if it is already on the ray arm.

GOAL: Move the core into the purple socket to unlock the purple button. CONTROLS: Arrows move the core; clicks activate buttons like the magenta teleporter. RULE: Pink cores act as teleport pads; the magenta button swaps the core between them. TRAP: Treating pink cores as simple collectibles wastes moves; they are essential transit points.

GOAL: Align two pieces and their reflections to cover two separate target shapes simultaneously. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected piece or shift the reflection offset. Space cycles through piece selection. RULE: Reflections mirror piece positions but share a single offset value that persists across piece changes. TRAP: Assuming each piece has an independent reflection offset; the shared offset means moving one affects the other’s reflection alignment.

GOAL: Guide the orange token to specific target cells while navigating around stationary red enemies. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the orange token two grid squares in the chosen direction per press. RULE: The orange token destroys a red enemy only if it lands directly on its square, not if it passes over or stops adjacent to it. TRAP: Assuming red enemies block movement or are destroyed by proximity; they are harmless obstacles unless you land exactly on them, causing wasted turns.

GOAL: Place a yellow block into the lower box to satisfy the win condition. CONTROLS: Red and green clicks shift the row of blocks horizontally to align items. RULE: Only the final state is checked; temporary loss of color in the upper box is acceptable. TRAP: Assuming both boxes must hold yellow simultaneously, which is impossible due to movement parity.

GOAL: Guide two players to the exit using mirrored controls. CONTROLS: Arrows move the right player directly and the left player inversely. RULE: Pressing a direction moves both players simultaneously based on their side. TRAP: Assuming one player moves alone causes collisions and wasted actions.

GOAL: Cover all target dots using a plus-shaped piece. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plus; pressing an arrow moves both arms unless blocked by the grid edge or a wall. RULE: If one arm hits a barrier, it stops while the other continues, allowing you to decouple their movement. TRAP: Assuming both arms always move together leads to dead ends; use barriers to park one arm while positioning the other.

GOAL: Move lines and the piece to cover all yellow cells. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the active item; Space switched between horizontal line, vertical line, and piece. RULE: The piece had to be placed exactly at the intersection of the two lines. TRAP: Assuming lines could stop anywhere; they only moved in fixed steps, requiring careful count to align.

GOAL: Slide the line to align gaps, then move both shapes to the left. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active object; Space cycles between line and shapes. RULE: Only the selected object moves; the cycle order is Line, Shapes. TRAP: Assuming shapes move together; they are independent objects requiring separate selection.

GOAL: Guide the core across a moving platform to the exit. CONTROLS: Arrows move the core; yellow shifts the platform; gray clears the floor barrier. RULE: The core must remain on the platform while it shifts right to reach the cleared zone. TRAP: Do not shift the platform if the core is near the edge, or it will fall when the platform moves.

GOAL: Fit all remaining pieces into their matching sockets. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected piece; clicks select a piece. RULE: A piece locks in only when fully aligned inside a socket’s inner boundary. TRAP: Assuming any visible overlap counts; slight misalignments prevent locking and waste moves.

GOAL: Align two scattered pieces to form a complete, contiguous shape on the grid. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the active selection; Space cycles through horizontal, vertical, and individual piece modes. RULE: The shape only locks when every cell of the target silhouette is covered by exactly one piece. TRAP: Assuming pieces move independently; they must be positioned relative to each other, not just the board edges.

GOAL: Move the large object to the left target using only the small green block. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the green block; moving into the large object pushes it. RULE: The green block stops when hitting walls or the large object, never overlapping. TRAP: Assuming the green block moves through the large object or pushes it indefinitely without stopping.

ESTABLISHED: Rotations change prong direction. Moves shift the plug by two cells. The budget is nearly exhausted. FAILED: Combinations of rotations and two-cell moves have not aligned the plug with the gate. GOAL IS NOT: Simple adjacency or partial contact is insufficient; exact alignment is required. CONTROLS: Toggles define column effects. The blob executes the sequence.

ESTABLISHED: Pegs exist on a grid and in a cart; clicking moves them. FAILED: Clicking various empty cells did not trigger a win. GOAL IS NOT: Eliminating all pegs or reaching a single peg. CONTROLS: Click a peg to select, then click a valid destination to move or jump over another peg to capture it.

ESTABLISHED: A small piston at the top-left creates the required diagonal band when pressed. Its bracket is partially hidden by the larger piston's housing. FAILED: Clicking the guessed location of the small bracket did nothing. GOAL IS NOT: Achieved by pressing the large piston alone. CONTROLS: Clicking a bracket presses that piston; the small piston's exact clickable area remains unidentified.

GOAL: Transform the grid pattern to match the target shape by navigating through mirror portals. CONTROLS: Arrows move the piece; entering a portal flips the grid pattern along a specific axis. RULE: Horizontal and vertical entries trigger different mirror flips, so combining them rotates the pattern. TRAP: Assuming horizontal entry causes a horizontal flip; it actually causes a vertical flip, confusing the logic.

ESTABLISHED: A dark red chaser and a red lunge tile exist. The red tile is lethal if approached in its facing direction. FAILED: Approaching the red tile directly from the west causes instant death. Navigating through the blocked chain below the red tile is impossible. GOAL IS NOT: Located behind the red tile or within the inaccessible chain region. CONTROLS: Moving into the red tile's ray triggers a lethal lunge. The chaser moves to intercept the player.

GOAL: Navigate the maze to reach the exit while evading a pursuing enemy. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the character one step in the selected direction. RULE: The pursuer always moved toward your current position, requiring constant movement to maintain distance. TRAP: Believing the pursuer moves instantly to your previous location caused unnecessary deaths; it actually lags one step behind.

GOAL: You must navigate through vertical water shafts to reach a pink goal located at the upper left of the map. CONTROLS: Use arrow keys to shift the player horizontally within water columns and click on corks to trigger a vertical rise. RULE: The player only rises when aligned directly beneath a cork, and the camera shifts immediately upon rising. TRAP: Do not assume the view stays static; clicking coordinates before the camera resets after a rise will cause you to miss the target.

ESTABLISHED: Four shapes must touch to form a single connected cluster. FAILED: Moving pieces independently without checking path overlaps causes jams. GOAL IS NOT: A simple visual match or color alignment. CONTROLS: Click a piece to select, then press direction keys to slide it until it hits a wall or another piece.

ESTABLISHED: Vertical and horizontal bars move as a connected cross; if one hits an obstacle, the other stops to keep them joined. FAILED: Pressing up when the horizontal bar is blocked results in no movement, confirming the strict connection rule. GOAL IS NOT: Moving the bars to arbitrary positions; they must cross at a specific target coordinate to align. CONTROLS: Directional inputs move the cross; movement is restricted by obstacles and the requirement that the bars remain intersected.

ESTABLISHED: The piston fits the window geometry if white reaches 46. FAILED: Pumping to equalize levels (55,55) opens the gate but does not push the piston through. GOAL IS NOT: Simply matching water levels to open the gate. CONTROLS: Clicking pumps raises white levels in the selected region.

GOAL: Guide the player to the exit while evading a sliding chaser that tracks you every turn. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move one step, but walls cause continuous sliding until stopping. RULE: The chaser always takes the shortest path toward your current position after your move. TRAP: Assuming the chaser stops at obstacles; it slides through gaps, so avoid aligning with clear lanes leading to you.

GOAL: Guide the plug through the narrow constriction to the exit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the plug; clicking keypad symbols enters the code. RULE: Entering the correct code shrinks the plug from four-by-four to two-by-two, allowing it to fit through tight channels. TRAP: Assuming the plug remains a fixed size; it must shrink to pass obstacles that block the larger form.

GOAL: Drive the plug into the blade's tip to unlock the exit. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plug; clicking keypad cells shrinks its size. RULE: A wide plug cannot pass through narrow channels, forcing you to shrink it first. TRAP: Believing the plug fits everywhere until hitting a wall wastes moves; check channel width before moving.

GOAL: Fit the yellow plus into the ring and park green blocks in squares. CONTROLS: Arrows slide the selected piece; clicks select the piece. RULE: Pieces slide until blocked, but can stop precisely when filling a matching target shape. TRAP: Assuming the ring outline was a solid wall prevented seeing the plus could slide fully inside.

ESTABLISHED: Timer is 27. Box at (6,12) is static. Path to it is clear. FAILED: Global step arithmetic for timer prediction was inconsistent. GOAL IS NOT: A simple straight-line path without collision avoidance. CONTROLS: Movement keys shift position; SPACE absorbs or places blocks; timer ticks per action.

GOAL: Move one box to its target spot within the time limit. CONTROLS: Arrows move your character; Space absorbs or places a box. RULE: Your character has two parts; both must be clear of obstacles and enemies during movement. TRAP: Assuming every action consumes exactly one timer unit; some actions do not advance the clock.

GOAL: Move the block through the rainbow until the panel turns blue. CONTROLS: Arrows slide the block one step in that direction. RULE: Each time the block enters the rainbow, the panel color cycles forward. TRAP: Thinking the rainbow color is fixed; it actually changes with every re-entry.

GOAL: Guide the plug to the handle at the bottom-left. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the plug four units in the pressed direction. RULE: The plug must fit entirely within open gray paths to move. TRAP: Assuming the plug could squeeze through narrow gaps or turn without clearing space.

ESTABLISHED: Max snake length is 35; vertical wall max reach is 44. Snake tip at 41 cannot cover target at 42. FAILED: Extending snake to 36 overlaps vertical wall. Horizontal wall covering second target overlaps purple block. GOAL IS NOT: Surviving on budget. CONTROLS: Clicking panel halves adjusts bar lengths. Clicking dividers to test rotation is unverified.

GOAL: Move the green block into the gray ring. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block three spaces; the plug shifts colors each turn. RULE: The block can only enter the ring when the plug’s bottom row is not red. TRAP: Believing the block pushes the plug; it actually teleports, so timing the color cycle is key.

ESTABLISHED: The invader chases the nearest square, forcing a choice between saving the piece or letting it be eaten. FAILED: Moving the main piece to the merge point while the invader is close, which causes immediate consumption. GOAL IS NOT: Ignoring the invader’s proximity or assuming it ignores the nearest target. CONTROLS: Clicking moves the selected piece; the invader moves toward the closest piece after every action.

ESTABLISHED: The gray square button changes the black bar's ends to walkable white cells. The goal region connects via the purple bar and white bar. FAILED: Walking directly across the charcoal gap between the start and lower-left regions. GOAL IS NOT: A simple straight-line walk from start to finish without manipulating the shutter or purple dashed piece. CONTROLS: The gray square button toggles the black bar's state, revealing walkable cells at its edges.
